assumptions: Spec and plan sign-off were taken without a human (fleet lane). The fleet orchestrator accepted the planner's concerns 1 to 5 and assumptions A2 to A11.

Approach A: the export composes saved outputs from local files and never reaches the network. Batwoman evidence comes from saved `canary batwoman --issue N --json` reports, by default under .canary/batwoman/.
The surface is the engine command `canary evidence export`, with no skill and no Birds of Prey name in v1.
The command is advisory: exit 0 with an Abstained warning line when no source produced an item, 2 on a usage error, 1 when the pack cannot be written.

Six catalogue rows: NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4 sections 2.3.3 and 2.3.4 (section numbers checked against the published PDF), ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.8, CIS Controls v8 Control 7 as one row naming Safeguards 7.2 and 7.7, SOC 2 CC7.1 and CC8.1. The ISO, CIS and SOC 2 descriptions are paraphrases.
A1: dated records use the half-open window [since, until); the single ci-ready item, dated at the export, is inside when since <= export time <= until.
A2: when every ci-ready check skipped the source is absent with the reason `no check scored`.
A3: ci-ready states are decided in the order out-of-window, unreadable (no HEAD), absent, read.
A4: out-of-window is used for ci-ready only; a file source with records but none in the window is read with zero items in the window.
A5: a record with a date but no identifier is not an item and makes its source partial.
A6: a date-time with no zone is a usage error.
A7: source paths in the pack are root-relative.
A8: a commit URL is built only from an owner/name slug and a full SHA; a --repo or GITHUB_REPOSITORY that is not a slug exits 2.
A9: a --batwoman path that exists but is not a directory is unreadable (ENOTDIR), not exit 2.
A10: items are ordered newest first, with source and id breaking ties.
A11: the catalogue is a JSON data file read at runtime.
Security review: commit URLs come only from the repository the caller gave; the fallback to a batwoman report's own repo field (spec D13 as first written) was withdrawn.

The pack omits run failure text. It keeps the ledger author and, for a row with no cause, the ledger's free-text reason, because the issue asks for an owner and a reason. Whether to replace them with a non-personal handle and the enumerated cause only is an open question for the maintainer.
The module layout differs from the first spec draft (files are written by render.ts and sources are run by pack.ts) to stay under the arch coupling ratio with no allowance.
docs/roadmap.md was edited by hand for the #855 row only, because manage_roadmap promote rewrote every row.
